m_treehouse.title: The Treehouse
m_treehouse.text: A small wooden door. A blanket fort lit by a flashlight. A voice, gentle, promising that no matter what happened downstairs, in here they would always be safe.
fragments: First — a small wooden door, pulled shut against the noise below.
Then the whole world shrank to a blanket fort, lit by one wavering flashlight.
And last, a voice — gentle, certain — promising that whatever happened downstairs, in here they would always be safe.

m_porch.title: The Porch
m_porch.text: Two kids on a cold porch step, sharing one coat. 'I've got you,' the older one whispered. Someone learned, very early, how to be the safe place for someone else.
fragments: First — two kids on a cold porch step, one coat shared between them.
Then the older one pulled it tighter and whispered, 'I've got you.'
And from that night on, someone had learned — far too early — how to be the safe place for someone else.

m_kitchen.title: The Kitchen Doorway
m_kitchen.text: A child in a doorway, learning the rhythm of the house — when it was safe to speak, when it was safer to go quiet and small. The first time someone steady stepped forward so the child wouldn't have to.
fragments: First — a child in a doorway, reading the rhythm of the house.
Then learning its rules: when it was safe to speak, and when it was safer to go quiet and small.
And the first time someone steadier stepped forward, so the child wouldn't have to.

m_first_words.title: The First 'We'
m_first_words.text: A page of a childhood journal, the handwriting changing halfway down. 'We' instead of 'I' — not a mistake, but a truce. The moment the inside ones agreed, quietly, to keep each other safe.
fragments: First — a page of a childhood journal, the handwriting changing halfway down.
Then a single word: 'we' in place of 'I' — not a slip, but a truce.
And in that moment the inside ones agreed, quietly, to keep one another safe.

m_whole.title: The Whole of It
m_whole.text: It comes together at last: the treehouse, the porch, the doorway, the first 'we'. Not one story but many, held by many — each part born to carry what one child couldn't carry alone. Not broken. Survived. Together.
fragments: First — the pieces drift back together: the treehouse, the porch, the doorway, the first 'we'.
Then they settle into one shape — not a single story, but many, held by many.
And each part, it turns out, was born to carry what one child could not carry alone.
